How to submit homework

To submit homework, go to the Homework page from the sidebar. Select the pending assignment you want to submit from the list on the left. Then drag and drop your file — a PDF, DOCX, or a photo of your handwritten work — into the upload box on the right, or click it to browse your files. Once your file is selected, click Submit Homework. You can track the status of all your submissions in the Homework Submission History table at the bottom of the page, including your score and any feedback once a teacher has graded it.

How to ask a doubt

If you're stuck on a concept, use the Doubt Forum from the sidebar to ask your teacher or classmates. Click New Doubt, choose the subject, write a clear title, and describe your question in detail. Once posted, teachers or other students can reply directly in the thread. You'll see all your open and resolved doubts listed, and you can reply to an existing thread if you have a follow-up question instead of creating a new one.

How to find study materials

Study materials uploaded by your teachers — notes, question papers, and reference documents — are available on the Study Materials page. You can browse materials by subject. Each entry shows the title, subject, and a preview of its content when the material has been processed for text search.

How self-evaluation works

The Self-Evaluation page gives you a personal view of your academic progress, including your homework completion rate, scores over time, and areas that may need more focus. This helps you track your own performance without waiting for a formal report.

Understanding your dashboard

Your Dashboard is the first page you see after logging in. It shows a quick summary of your pending homework count, unresolved doubts, and recent activity — including your latest homework submissions and doubt forum posts — so you always know what needs your attention.

How to reset your password

If you forget your password, click Forgot Password on the login page. Enter the email address associated with your account, and you'll receive instructions to reset your password. Follow the link in that message to set a new password.

Study Notes: Algebra (MATHEMATICS)

This material covers the core concepts of Algebra as taught in the MATHEMATICS curriculum.

Key areas covered:
- Fundamental definitions and terminology related to Algebra
- Worked examples demonstrating standard problem-solving approaches for Algebra
- Common mistakes students make when studying Algebra, and how to avoid them
- Practice problems with step-by-step solutions

Students who are struggling with Algebra specifically should focus on the worked
examples section first, then attempt the practice problems independently before
checking solutions. Revisit the fundamental definitions if the practice problems
feel unfamiliar — a weak grasp of Algebra's core terminology is the most common
root cause of difficulty in this area.
